transcript:
Header:
- Date/Time: 2028-11-05 09:23 PT
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE), Jordan Price (Nimbus Head of ML), Asha Patel (Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (SRE)

Summary: quick console walkthrough concentrating on tracing, error analysis, request logs, and debugging flows. Customer wants to understand how to triage high-p95 latency, identify model fallbacks and see what data is retained/exported for compliance.

Topics: tracing spans, request logs, sampling, error analysis panel, filters by model/route, PV vs hosted concerns, log retention & S3 export, KMS/SSO questions

Transcript:
[00:00] Samantha: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm samantha with redwood — i'll hand off to carlos in a bit for the console deep dive but quick agenda, show tracing, error analysis, request logs, and then q&a.
[00:18] Jordan: yeah great thanks, we're mostly interested in debugging flows. we've been seeing periodic p95 spikes on a couple inference routes, curious what you can show us.
[00:30] Carlos: cool, i'll share my screen — lemme know if you can't see it. so this is the console home, we're in the tracing tab, top left you can pick time-range, model, deployment. you can also filter by route or API key.
[01:05] Asha: when you say route, do you mean our application routes or redwood routes?
[01:12] Carlos: good call — it's the redwood route key which you can map to your app-level route in metadata. we add a route label at request time, so you can group by feature, e.g., chat-completion / summary / rerank.
[01:30] Liam: and is trace sampling on by default? we don't want to ingest everything for cost reasons.
[01:36] Samantha: yep sampling is configurable per-account and per-deployment. default is adaptive: higher sample rate for errors and higher latency requests. you can also force sample for a specific session id.
[01:55] Carlos: walking through a trace now — top-level view shows timeline with spans for network, model, token-generation, kv-cache hit/miss. note: model runtime span is broken down by kernel time vs queue/wait time, which helps distinguish infra vs model.
[02:30] Jordan: i see a lot of "kv cache" hits but some misses — how precise is that? sometimes in our system names like k-v cache get transcribed oddly.
[02:42] Carlos: ha, the console label might show kv-cache or kv cache — but the underlying tag is consistent. the hit rate is computed per-request; you can click a span to see the raw request/response payload (redacted by default for PII).
[03:10] Asha: redacted by default — can we export unredacted logs to our S3? for a pilot we need full payloads behind our KMS.
[03:21] Samantha: yes, for Dedicated/Private deployments you can enable full retention and export to your S3, and keys are wrapped using your KMS. for hosted we offer masked by default and a controlled unredacted export workflow when approved.
[03:45] Carlos: back to the trace — you can also create a span-level filter, e.g., show only spans where model latency > 300ms or where model fallback occurred. fallback events are tagged as "model_variant_fallback" so you can find routes that hit smaller models under load.
[04:10] Jordan: can we correlate fallback events with cost? like which requests landed on quantized variant and how that changes token cost.
[04:22] Carlos: yes, the request log entries include model_variant and billing_tokens. in the request logs panel you can pivot by model_variant and sum billing tokens to get cost impact. we also show token-level cost breakdown in the tracing when available.
[04:45] Liam: what about privacy/audit — do you keep a log of who viewed logs and traces?
[04:52] Samantha: audit logs are built-in; every access to request logs or trace payloads is recorded with user id, IP, and action. that's separate from request logs and can be exported to your SIEM.
[05:18] Carlos: switching to error analysis — this view aggregates exceptions and error codes across routes, groups by root cause suggestions like "payload-invalid", "timeout", or "model-oom". you can drill into a grouped error and see sample traces and example inputs.
[05:45] Jordan: what's the granularity of error grouping? we've got some noisy upstream validation errors that mask real model failures.
[05:53] Carlos: grouping is configurable; default is cluster by similarity of stack and error message, but you can add custom anomaly rules — e.g., ignore validation errors from our preprocessor by route label.
[06:15] Asha: can we set alerts off the error groups? an automated alert for when model-ooms spike beyond N/hour?
[06:23] Samantha: yes alerting ties into our Rollouts and Ops; you can create thresholds on the error group or set a detection rule with automatic Slack or PagerDuty notifications.
[06:40] Carlos: now the request logs — think of it as a raw event store for every request, searchable by trace_id, user_id, model, and headers. by default we index a set of metadata fields and keep raw payloads for X days depending on plan.
[07:05] Liam: X days =?
[07:07] Samantha: hosted default 30 days for raw payloads, 90 days for metadata indexes. Dedicated customers can extend retention and we support cold storage exports. Private deployments you control retention.
[07:25] Jordan: ok, if we need longer for audits, can we push to our bucket?
[07:30] Samantha: yes S3 export with lifecycle rules is supported. we also support streaming to Splunk/Datadog via integrations.
[07:46] Carlos: demo: search for a trace id — typing "trace: 7f2b..." shows the trace, then the right-hand pane shows timeline, raw request/response (redacted), and buttons: export JSON, copy trace link, open in error analysis.
[08:15] Jordan: I notice the timeline shows a big queue time. does the console show queue length or GPU utilization?
[08:22] Carlos: we surface queue depth by deployment instance and GPU utilization by node in the infra tab — you can correlate a trace to the instance id that served it. for privacy we only show IDs, but in Dedicated you get full node telemetry.
[08:45] Asha: curious about cross-region fallbacks — we are multi-region and want requests to failover gracefully if a region saturates.
[08:54] Samantha: smart routing policy will try in-region, then fall back to nearest region or to cheaper capacity tier depending on your policy. traces will show cross-region hop as an additional span.
[09:15] Liam: we've got compliance concerns — SOC 2 + customer-managed keys. are those already in your compliance pack?
[09:22] Samantha: yes SOC2 Type II is in our pack, we also support customer-managed KMS keys for Dedicated and Private. i'll attach the compliance pack after the call.
[09:36] Carlos: another useful feature — the console can run a "replay" for a given trace against a non-prod model variant, so you can reproduce a failing request without touching production traffic. you can also scrub PII during replay.
[09:58] Jordan: does replay preserve prefixes and kv-cache state?
[10:04] Carlos: good question — we attempt to reconstruct KV cache when available; for long-running sessions you might get partial cache, but our replay tool can seed a cache snapshot if you collected it. that is available in Dedicated/private setups.
[10:25] Asha: on the topic of KV cache and quantization — we have a mixed workload with short chat + long document summarization. does your tracing attribute token-generation cost across segments?
[10:38] Carlos: yep per-span token counts are shown. you can filter to only the generation spans and get token delta per span. this helps with hybrid workloads to see which stage is expensive.
[10:55] Samantha: and Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per-route to reduce cost while keeping quality; that's a separate module but ties into traces for validation.
[11:10] Jordan: hmm ok, for our SREs we want a runbook: when p95 spikes, step 1 look at traces, step 2 look at model fallbacks, step 3 check infra, step 4 escalate. can you export a snapshot that contains all that context?
[11:25] Carlos: you can export a consolidated incident bundle — trace, logs, infra metrics, and links to sample inputs — bundle is a zip with JSON manifests and optional redacted/unredacted payloads per policy.
[11:40] Liam: are those bundles consumable by our incident tool (we use PagerDuty + internal ticketing)?
[11:45] Carlos: yes there's an API to push bundles to a URL or integrate with PagerDuty runbook links.
[11:55] Asha: about data residency — we need EU only for certain customers. can we restrict logs and traces to eu-west-1?
[12:03] Samantha: absolutely, you can set region pinning per-tenant and we ensure logs and raw payloads stay in that region. for multi-tenant accounts you can create subtenants with their own residency.
[12:22] Jordan: back to a demo step — show me a recent error group that led to model-oom.
[12:28] Carlos: clicking error group, here's a cluster of OOMs from last night, sample traces show token window exceeded and model_oom. we display stack and memory estimate when model reports it. you can click to open in the model profiler for per-layer memory breakdown (note: profiler requires enabled runtime hooks).
[12:55] Jordan: runtime hooks — is that intrusive? does it add latency?
[13:00] Carlos: the profiler sampling has a tiny overhead, we do low-frequency sampling by default. it's off by default on hosted but available for dedicated with opt-in.
[13:14] Liam: when you talk about "enabled runtime hooks" is that something we install or config?
[13:20] Samantha: it's an agent-level opt-in; in private/dedicated you can enable it via your deployment config and the binary includes the hooks.
[13:32] Asha: okay let's talk about RBAC — we need least-priv access so engineers can't see unredacted payloads.
[13:38] Samantha: RBAC supports role templates and custom roles. you can restrict access to request logs, to trace payloads, and enable just-in-time approval for unredacted views. audit trail captured.
[13:55] Carlos: demonstration: create a role called "sre-readonly" and toggle request_log.view = false and trace.view = true, saving role is immediate. you can attach it to SSO groups.
[14:15] Jordan: you mentioned SSO — SAML + OIDC?
[14:18] Samantha: both, SAML for enterprise, OIDC for platform apps. we also support SCIM for provisioning.
[14:30] Asha: latency breakdown — can we generate a per-route p50/p95 chart for the last 7 days and overlay deployment changes?
[14:38] Carlos: yes time-series panel supports overlays like deployment version, quantization change, or routing policy changes. you can annotate the timeline with deploy tags.
[14:57] Liam: sometimes our app does retries; can you correlate downstream retries to original requests to avoid double-counting?
[15:05] Carlos: we propagate a client_request_id header; the console groups by original id when present and will show deduplication stats. we recommend instrumenting that header.
[15:22] Jordan: regarding cost telemetry, your token-level breakdown — is that aligned to our billing window? we have to match accounting.
[15:30] Samantha: billing tokens are exported with timestamps and invoice IDs if you sync billing; you can reconcile by summing billing_tokens across request logs in the invoice period. API also exists for programmatic fetch.
[15:50] Carlos: quick demo of debugging flow — find a spike at 03:14 UTC, filter by route "summarize-v2" and latency > 1s, select sample trace, open replay, choose non-prod model, run replay. it reproduces the long latency which points to a model variant fallback under load.
[16:25] Asha: could the fallback be due to warmup or cold cache?
[16:29] Carlos: yes, the trace shows a big kv-cache miss preceding fallback. we have a prewarm option that keeps hot prefixes in memory, and you can pin prefixes for critical flows.
[16:45] Jordan: what about continuous exporting for ML teams — we want nightly dumps of request logs for offline evals.
[16:52] Samantha: scheduled exports are supported — daily or hourly dumps to your bucket with retention rules. you can also export only metadata or full payload.
[17:10] Liam: do you redact things automatically like SSNs?
[17:14] Carlos: we provide PII redaction rules and regex-based scrubbing; customers can add custom rules.
[17:28] Jordan: ok quick callout — we need to run a pilot testing model fallbacks under synthetic load and measure p95 impact. what do you need from us?
[17:36] Samantha: would like three things: a sample route and dataset, expected SLO/targets, and a rough expected qps pattern. carlos will propose a benchmark plan.
[17:46] Carlos: i'll put together a plan — we'll run a controlled synthetic test and produce an incident bundle for each anomaly we inject so you can validate replay and traces.
[18:00] Asha: security question — are request logs encrypted at rest?
[18:04] Samantha: yes AES-256 at rest; for Dedicated/Private we support CMEK via your KMS.
[18:12] Liam: how long to enable Dedicated for a pilot if we want isolated capacity?
[18:18] Samantha: smallest Dedicated pilot can be provisioned in 2-4 weeks typically, depending on procurement and network onboarding. Private on-prem takes longer.
[18:30] Jordan: procurement will ask about SLA and data deletion procedures.
[18:34] Samantha: standard SLA and documented deletion workflows are in the compliance pack i'll share. are there other questions?
[18:45] Asha: one more: can we mask input tokens before storing but keep enough context for debugging?
[18:50] Carlos: yes you can apply token-level redaction rules that replace sensitive spans with placeholders but still keep token counts and positional context.
[19:05] Jordan: nice. on trials — pricing for pilot with 8k qps bursts and 100k daily tokens?
[19:12] Samantha: i'll send pilot pricing options; quick note, cost depends on model_family, quantization, and dedicated vs hosted. i'll include a pricing spreadsheet.
[19:28] Carlos: back to console features — you can create saved queries for common investigations and share them with teammates; saved queries include filters, date range, and selected spans.
[19:45] Liam: saved queries + role-based sharing would help oncall runbooks.
[19:51] Carlos: yep; we also have short runbook templates you can attach to a saved query.
[20:05] Jordan: ok let's do a short live exercise — try to find last 5 errors for route "chat-async".
[20:10] Carlos: applying filter route:chat-async and error:true, time range last 24h — results, grouping shows 5 errors, clicking group shows example traces, opening one shows payload and stack.
[20:40] Asha: can we link this to our ticketing system directly?
[20:44] Carlos: yes, use the export to URL webhook to push a bundle to a connector that creates a ticket.
[20:52] Jordan: anything else on observability integrations?
[20:55] Samantha: Datadog, Prometheus, Splunk, and generic webhook. you can stream infra metrics to your existing dashboards.
[21:10] Liam: curious about overhead — do your traces add headers to every request?
[21:16] Carlos: minimal trace header is injected by the SDK or proxy; it's a small header and we support sampling to reduce volume.
[21:30] Jordan: right now we instrument via a proxy so adding headers should be straightforward.
[21:36] Samantha: recap next steps: we'll send compliance pack, pricing sheet, and sample benchmark plan. carlos will own benchmark plan, i will own security/docs and pricing.
[21:50] Carlos: i'll follow up with a sample replay runbook and ask for sample trace ids.
[22:00] Asha: jordan and i will share a small dataset and top failing routes.
[22:06] Liam: procurement will reach out for SLA question, expect an email.
[22:12] Samantha: perfect. anything else before we close?
[22:18] Jordan: no that's it, thanks for the walkthrough.
[22:22] Samantha: thanks everyone, we'll send notes and links.
[22:30] End of recording.

Notes: Transcript includes small transcription artifacts and inconsistent punctuation. Several product names and internal terms may be slightly off (kv-cache vs k v cache). The call concluded with clear next steps and three action items assigned.
